# Verification, Failure Detection & Recovery

> "Exit codes" for robots: success detection, failure reasoning, self-reflection, recovery and knowing when to ask for help.  
> Layer: L5 · 43 entries · [overview](../README.md#verification) · [survey](../SURVEY.md)

**Legend:** 🟢 open · 🟡 partial · 🔵 api · ⚪ closed. Hover a name for the full paper title. Newest first within each year.

**2026**

- 🟢 [**SAGE**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34268 "SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners") · 2026-09 — LLM task planner with a model-free symbolic gate that blocks precondition-violating actions with typed reasons before actuation, plus a local edit that regenerates only the failed sub-goal's suffix; evaluated on a 75-task AI2-THOR benchmark and on a Jetson AGX Orin. [code](https://github.com/mtbui2010/sage_release)
- ⚪ [**ROBORMBENCH**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05401 "Same Trajectory, Contradictory Rewards (ROBORMBENCH): Paraphrase Fragility in Vision Language Reward Models") · 2026-09 · Yonsei University et al. — Paraphrase-robustness benchmark for VLM reward models: 2,390 real-robot trajectories with progress labels and 21,673 verified instruction paraphrases; rewording alone can flip identical behavior between judged success and failure.
- ⚪ [**GAVEL**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19315 "GAVEL: Graph World Models for Verified and Efficient Long-Horizon LLM Task Planning") · 2026-09 — Verifies and repairs LLM task plans against an explicit graph world model of object relations, action preconditions/effects and beliefs over unseen object locations: it predicts consequences before execution, fixes violations directly and saves LLM replanning for semantic errors. _Note: First-party: on BEHAVIOR-1K, Qwen3-8B single-task success rises from 41.2% to 91.8%._
- ⚪ [**FailBench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03611 "FailBench: How Reliable are VLMs at Judging Robot Task Success?") · 2026-09 — Benchmark of 2,197 manipulation attempts from 14 public sources for VLM success/failure judges; the best of 13 detectors reaches 0.77 mean balanced accuracy, near chance on contact-rich assembly, with a bias toward predicting success. _Note: First-party numbers; a direct check on VLM-as-judge reliability._ [project](https://metric-ai-lab.github.io/failbench/)
- ⚪ [**F4R**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35575 "F4R: Failure-Driven Recognition, Reconstruction, Refinement, and Redeployment for Continual Robot Self-Improvement") · 2026-09 — Closed real-to-sim-to-real loop for VLA self-improvement: an agent detects and diagnoses real-world failures, each failure is rebuilt as an interactive simulated scene, the policy is refined with sim-real co-training and targeted RL, then redeployed.
- 🟡 [**CARE**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24118 "CARE: Experience-Guided Atomic Corrective Execution for Vision-Language-Action Policies") · 2026-09 — Learns VLA recovery from the policy's own failed rollouts: models stage-conditioned post-failure deviations to synthesize failure states and corrective demos, then uses stage-wise planning and 3D monitoring to trigger atomic adjustments at run time; adds the FSR-Bench recovery benchmark. _Note: The repo is a code-only snapshot; checkpoints and datasets are not included._ [code](https://github.com/xiaojunlan/care)
- ⚪ [**ARS**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34484 "ARS: Agentic Reward System for Robot Learning") · 2026-09 — Training-free progress reward modeling with general VLMs: a sub-agent proposes a task-relevant event timeline that a primary agent verifies and revises before estimating per-frame progress; it can also audit other reward models' progress estimates. _Note: The code URL given in the paper (github.com/midea-ai/ars) returned 404 on 2026-09-29._
- ⚪ [**ActionGround**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33256 "ActionGround: Training-Free Runtime Refinement of Frozen VLA Policies") · 2026-09 — Training-free runtime layer that wraps a frozen VLA without weight access: a phase-aware finite-state machine applies per-phase rule-based corrections, and an Euler-Lagrange term adds rigid-body dynamics to each control step, logging its residual as a diagnostic. _Note: Evaluated on LIBERO-Spatial and Robosuite pick-and-place; the real-arm trial is qualitative._
- 🟢 [**RynnValue**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09853 "RynnValue: Scaling Robotic Value Foundation Models with Temporal Distance") · 2026-08 · Alibaba DAMO Academy — Open value foundation model for manipulation that learns temporal distance (cost-to-go to a language goal) from timestamps over roughly 7,000 hours of clips, yielding progress estimates without preference or progress labels. [code](https://github.com/alibaba-damo-academy/RynnValue) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/Alibaba-DAMO-Academy/RynnValue-8B)
- ⚪ [**Semantic handoff failures**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06256 "Diagnosing Semantic Handoff Failures in Agent-Orchestrated Vision-Language-Action Skill Composition") · 2026-07 — Studies an agent-orchestrated harness that calls pi0.5-based BEHAVIOR-1K skills with typed arguments, step budgets and multi-view VLM verification; skills that succeed from clean snapshots often stall from states left by the previous skill.
- ⚪ [**Hide-and-Seek**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30834 "Hide-and-Seek in Trajectories: Discovering Failure Signals for VLA Runtime Monitoring") · 2026-05 · University of Wisconsin-Madison, Georgia Tech — Learns step-level failure signals for VLA runtime monitoring from trajectory-level success labels via inter- and intra-trajectory contrastive objectives, with conformal thresholds; evaluated with OpenVLA, pi0 and pi0.5 on LIBERO, VLABench and a real robot. _Note: NeurIPS 2026; official repo (deeplearning-wisc/hide_and_seek) says code is coming soon._ [project](https://seongheon-96.github.io/hide_and_seek_site/)
- 🟢 [**AgentChord**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11951 "From Reaction to Anticipation: Proactive Failure Recovery through Agentic Task Graph for Robotic Manipulation") · 2026-05 · CUHK-Shenzhen, DexForce — Multi-agent system that compiles a manipulation task into a directed task graph, pre-attaches anticipatory recovery branches, and uses low-latency monitors to fire pre-compiled recoveries without re-planning; shown on long-horizon bimanual tasks. _Note: RSS 2026._ [code](https://github.com/EDEM-AI/AgentChord) · [project](https://shengxu.net/AgentChord/)
- ⚪ [**SERP**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02772 "Self-Evolutionary Replanning for Failure-Aware Motion Planning") · 2026-03 · University of Macau; University of Hong Kong et al. — Failure-aware adaptation of motion-planner parameters and loss weights: auto-differentiation handles local updates while a VLM reads the adaptation history to intervene, and a memory-augmented rollout system proposes and tests recovery candidates.
- 🟢 [**Robometer**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02115 "Robometer: Scaling General-Purpose Robotic Reward Models via Trajectory Comparisons") · 2026-03 — General robot reward model trained with a frame-level progress loss on expert data plus a trajectory-comparison preference loss that exploits failed and suboptimal rollouts; releases RBM-1M, a reward-learning dataset of over one million trajectories. _Note: RSS 2026._ [code](https://github.com/robometer/robometer) · [project](https://robometer.github.io/) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/robometer/Robometer-4B)
- 🟢 [**PRM-as-a-Judge**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21669 "PRM-as-a-Judge: A Dense Evaluation Paradigm for Fine-Grained Robotic Auditing") · 2026-03 — Uses process reward models to audit policy rollout videos as dense progress curves scored by an Outcome-Process-Diagnosis metric system instead of binary success; ships the RoboPulse diagnostic benchmark and an open evaluator toolkit. _Note: Toolkit follow-up 'PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5' is arXiv 2608.14284 (2026-08)._ [code](https://github.com/YuyangLiu2003/PRM-as-a-Judge) · [project](https://prm-as-a-judge.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**CoVer-VLA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12281 "Scaling Verification Can Be More Effective than Scaling Policy Learning for Vision-Language-Action Alignment") · 2026-02 · Stanford University, NVIDIA Research — Trains CoVer, a contrastive verifier of instruction-action alignment, and uses it in a hierarchical test-time pipeline that scores VLM-rephrased instructions and sampled action chunks; reports larger gains than scaling policy pre-training on the same data. _Note: First-party results on SIMPLER, PolaRiS and real robots._ [code](https://github.com/cover-vla/cover-vla) · [project](https://cover-vla.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**RoboReward**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00675 "RoboReward: General-Purpose Vision-Language Reward Models for Robotics") · 2026-01 · Stanford University, UC Berkeley — Reward dataset and benchmark built from Open X-Embodiment and RoboArena episodes, using counterfactual relabeling and temporal clipping to create negatives, plus 4B/8B VLM reward models deployed for real-robot RL. _Note: First-party: the 8B model beats much larger general VLMs at short-horizon reward assignment and outperforms Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5 as an RL reward._ [project](https://crfm.stanford.edu/helm/robo-reward-bench/latest/) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/teetone/RoboReward-8B) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/teetone/RoboReward)
- 🟢 [**CycleVLA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02295 "CycleVLA: Proactive Self-Correcting Vision-Language-Action Models via Subtask Backtracking and Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding") · 2026-01 · University of Oxford — A progress-aware VLA flags risky subtask transitions, a VLM failure predictor triggers subtask backtracking, and Minimum Bayes Risk decoding improves retries; evaluated on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus and a real robot. [code](https://github.com/dannymcy/cyclevla_code) · [project](https://dannymcy.github.io/cyclevla/)

**2025**

- 🟢 [**Robo-Dopamine**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23703 "Robo-Dopamine: General Process Reward Modeling for High-Precision Robotic Manipulation") · 2025-12 · BAAI, Peking University — Step-aware, multi-view general process reward model trained on 3,400+ hours of data, paired with policy-invariant reward shaping (Dopamine-RL) for real-robot RL and one-shot adaptation to new tasks. _Note: Robo-Dopamine 2.0 (arXiv 2608.15680, 2026-08) adds history conditioning and OOD awareness._ [code](https://github.com/FlagOpen/Robo-Dopamine) · [project](https://robo-dopamine.github.io/) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/collections/tanhuajie2001/robo-dopamine)
- 🟢 [**Guardian**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01946 "Guardian: Detecting Robotic Planning and Execution Errors with Vision-Language Models") · 2025-12 · Inria, ENS-PSL — Perturbs successful RLBench and BridgeData V2 trajectories into planning and execution failures with VLM-written reasoning traces (GuardianFail-36k) and trains a multi-view reasoning VLM that verifies both plans and execution steps. [code](https://github.com/paulpacaud/Guardian-FailCot) · [project](https://www.di.ens.fr/willow/research/guardian/) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/collections/paulpacaud/robotic-failure-detection-dataset-and-model-guardian)
- 🟡 [**SEAL**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.16281 "Do What You Say: Steering Vision-Language-Action Models via Runtime Reasoning-Action Alignment Verification") · 2025-10 · NVIDIA, Carnegie Mellon University — Training-free runtime steering for reasoning VLAs: samples several action sequences, predicts their outcomes in simulation, and has a VLM pick the one whose outcome best matches the model's own textual plan; adds a reasoning-annotated LIBERO-100 extension. _Note: Code and data released; model checkpoints marked TBA in the repo._ [code](https://github.com/NVlabs/actalign) · [project](https://yilin-wu98.github.io/steering-reasoning-vla/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/libero-r-datasets)
- 🟡 [**FailSafe**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01642 "FailSafe: Reasoning and Recovery from Failures in Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2025-10 — Generates diverse failure cases paired with executable recovery actions in simulators with motion-planning support, then fine-tunes FailSafe-VLM (LLaVA-OV-7B) to detect failures and propose recoveries for VLAs such as pi0-FAST and OpenVLA in ManiSkill. _Note: IROS 2026. Repo covers failure/recovery data generation; a FailSafe-VLM checkpoint was not located._ [code](https://github.com/Jimntu/FailSafe_code) · [project](https://jimntu.github.io/FailSafe/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/onepiece1999/failsafe_data)
- 🟢 [**VLAC**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.15937 "A Vision-Language-Action-Critic Model for Robotic Real-World Reinforcement Learning") · 2025-09 · Shanghai AI Laboratory — InternVL-based process reward model that, given paired observations and a language goal, outputs dense progress deltas and a done signal (and can also emit actions); drives an asynchronous real-world RL loop with graded human-in-the-loop interventions. [code](https://github.com/InternRobotics/VLAC) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/InternRobotics/VLAC)
- 🟢 [**SARM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25358 "SARM: Stage-Aware Reward Modeling for Long Horizon Robot Manipulation") · 2025-09 · Stanford University, UC Berkeley, xdof — Video reward model that jointly predicts task stage and within-stage progress from language subtask annotations, used for Reward-Aligned Behavior Cloning that filters and reweights demonstrations (e.g. T-shirt folding); integrated into LeRobot. _Note: SARM2 (arXiv 2606.10305, 2026-06) extends it to multi-task stage-aware reward modeling._ [code](https://github.com/xdofai/opensarm) · [project](https://qianzhong-chen.github.io/sarm.github.io/) · [docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/lerobot/sarm)
- 🟢 [**I-FailSense**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.16072 "I-FailSense: Towards General Robotic Failure Detection with Vision-Language Models") · 2025-09 · Sorbonne Universite (ISIR) — Post-trains a VLM and attaches lightweight classifier heads to several internal layers, ensembled, to detect semantic-misalignment failures (a plausible action that does not match the instruction), using datasets derived from existing manipulation data. _Note: ICRA 2026._ [code](https://github.com/clemgris/I-FailSense) · [project](https://clemgris.github.io/I-FailSense/) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/collections/ACIDE/failsense-3b)
- 🟢 [**SAFE**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09937 "SAFE: Multitask Failure Detection for Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2025-06 · University of Toronto, Vector Institute, Toyota Research Institute — Learns a failure score from a VLA's internal features that generalises to unseen tasks, with conformal thresholds for timely stop/backtrack/ask-for-help alerts; tested on OpenVLA, pi0 and pi0-FAST in simulation and the real world. _Note: NeurIPS 2025._ [code](https://github.com/vla-safe/SAFE) · [project](https://vla-safe.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**RoboMonkey**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.17811 "RoboMonkey: Scaling Test-Time Sampling and Verification for Vision-Language-Action Models") · 2025-06 · Stanford University, UC Berkeley — Test-time scaling for VLAs: samples and perturbs candidate actions, then a VLM-based action verifier trained on synthetic preference data selects one; reports that action error follows a power law in the number of samples. _Note: CoRL 2025._ [code](https://github.com/robomonkey-vla/RoboMonkey) · [project](https://robomonkey-vla.github.io/) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/robomonkey-vla/monkey-verifier-7b)
- 🟢 [**RoboFAC**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.12224 "RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction") · 2025-05 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University — Failure-centric dataset (9,440 erroneous trajectories, 78k QA pairs, sim and real) and a lightweight VLM for task understanding, failure analysis and correction, used as an external supervisor in a real-world VLA control pipeline. [code](https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/RoboFAC) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/MINT-SJTU/RoboFAC-7B) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/MINT-SJTU/RoboFAC-dataset)
- ⚪ [**Ask-to-Act**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00907 "Grounding Multimodal LLMs to Embodied Agents that Ask for Help with Reinforcement Learning") · 2025-04 · Georgia Tech, Meta FAIR — Defines the Ask-to-Act task, where a household agent given under-specified rearrangement instructions must ask minimal clarification questions, and fine-tunes an MLLM as a VLA policy with online RL on LLM-generated rewards.
- 🟢 [**FAIL-Detect**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08558 "Can We Detect Failures Without Failure Data? Uncertainty-Aware Runtime Failure Detection for Imitation Learning Policies") · 2025-03 · Toyota Research Institute — Two-stage runtime failure detector trained only on successful demonstrations: policy inputs/outputs are distilled into uncertainty scores, and conformal prediction calibrates alarm thresholds for diffusion/flow policies. _Note: RSS 2025._ [code](https://github.com/CXU-TRI/FAIL-Detect) · [project](https://cxu-tri.github.io/FAIL-Detect-Website/)
- 🟢 [**ReflectVLM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16707 "Reflective Planning: Vision-Language Models for Multi-Stage Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation") · 2025-02 · Cornell University, CUHK, Yale University, UC Berkeley — Test-time reflection loop in which a VLM planner imagines future states with a generative model, uses them to pick actions and critiques its own choices; improves multi-stage manipulation over commercial VLMs and MCTS (first-party). [code](https://github.com/yunhaif/reflect-vlm) · [project](https://reflect-vlm.github.io/) · [weights](https://huggingface.co/collections/yunhaif/reflectvlm-67b95e4316ab2d5f71ad4b25)
- 🟢 [**FOREWARN**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01828 "From Foresight to Forethought: VLM-In-the-Loop Policy Steering via Latent Alignment") · 2025-02 · Carnegie Mellon University — A latent world model predicts the outcomes of candidate action plans from a generative policy, and a VLM aligned to those latents judges them in language, acting as an open-vocabulary runtime verifier for policy steering. [code](https://github.com/CMU-IntentLab/Forewarn) · [project](https://yilin-wu98.github.io/forewarn/)

**2024**

- ⚪ [**Code-as-Monitor**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04455 "Code-as-Monitor: Constraint-aware Visual Programming for Reactive and Proactive Robotic Failure Detection") · 2024-12 · Beihang University, Peking University, BAAI, Galbot — Casts reactive and proactive failure detection as spatio-temporal constraint satisfaction: a VLM writes monitor code over compact geometric "constraint elements", evaluated in real time to close the loop around open-loop policies. _Note: CVPR 2025. No code link on the project page._ [project](https://zhoues.github.io/Code-as-Monitor/)
- ⚪ [**GVL**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04549 "Vision Language Models are In-Context Value Learners") · 2024-11 · Google DeepMind — Generative Value Learning prompts a VLM to predict task progress over shuffled video frames, giving zero/few-shot value estimates on 300+ real-world tasks that can be used for success detection, dataset filtering and advantage-weighted regression. _Note: No official code; the OpenGVL benchmark (arXiv 2509.17321) re-implements GVL with open VLMs._ [project](https://generative-value-learning.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**V-GPS**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13816 "Steering Your Generalists: Improving Robotic Foundation Models via Value Guidance") · 2024-10 · UC Berkeley, Carnegie Mellon University — Deployment-time steering that samples actions from a generalist robot policy and re-ranks them with a value function learned by offline RL, improving five different policies without fine-tuning or access to their weights. _Note: CoRL 2024. Early 'verifier re-ranks policy samples' pattern later scaled by RoboMonkey and CoVer-VLA._ [code](https://github.com/nakamotoo/V-GPS) · [project](https://nakamotoo.github.io/V-GPS/)
- 🟢 [**Sentinel**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.04640 "Unpacking Failure Modes of Generative Policies: Runtime Monitoring of Consistency and Progress") · 2024-10 · Stanford University, NVIDIA Research — Runtime monitor for diffusion policies that pairs a cheap statistical temporal action consistency test for erratic failures with a VLM that flags task-progression failures; evaluated on simulated and real mobile manipulation. _Note: CoRL 2024._ [code](https://github.com/agiachris/sentinel) · [project](https://sites.google.com/stanford.edu/sentinel)
- 🟡 [**AHA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00371 "AHA: A Vision-Language-Model for Detecting and Reasoning Over Failures in Robotic Manipulation") · 2024-10 · NVIDIA, University of Washington — Instruction-tuned VLM that detects manipulation failures and explains them in free-form language, trained on FailGen data made by perturbing successful simulated demos; its feedback is plugged into reward design, TAMP and sub-task verification. _Note: ICLR 2025. Repo has data-generation and fine-tuning code; no released AHA checkpoint was found._ [code](https://github.com/NVlabs/AHA) · [project](https://aha-vlm.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**RACER**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.14674 "RACER: Rich Language-Guided Failure Recovery Policies for Imitation Learning") · 2024-09 · University of Michigan — Supervisor-actor framework: a VLM supervisor issues rich language corrections to a language-conditioned visuomotor policy trained on demonstrations automatically augmented with failure-recovery trajectories; evaluated on RLBench and a real robot. [code](https://github.com/sled-group/RACER) · [project](https://rich-language-failure-recovery.github.io/) · [data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/sled-umich/RACER-augmented_rlbench)
- 🟢 [**IntroPlan**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06529 "Introspective Planning: Aligning Robots' Uncertainty with Inherent Task Ambiguity") · 2024-02 · Princeton University — Retrieves introspective reasoning examples (post-hoc rationales of human-chosen safe plans) at run time so an LLM planner's uncertainty tracks instruction ambiguity; combined with conformal prediction it cuts unnecessary clarification requests. _Note: NeurIPS 2024; adds a safe mobile manipulation benchmark._ [code](https://github.com/kevinliang888/IntroPlan) · [project](https://introplan.github.io/)

**2023**

- 🟢 [**KnowNo**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.01928 "Robots That Ask For Help: Uncertainty Alignment for Large Language Model Planners") · 2023-07 · Princeton University, Google DeepMind — Applies conformal prediction to an LLM planner's candidate next steps to obtain a statistical task-success guarantee; when the prediction set holds more than one option the robot asks a human for help, minimising help requests. _Note: CoRL 2023 oral. Canonical 'ask for help' exit code for LLM planners._ [code](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/language_model_uncertainty) · [project](https://robot-help.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**DoReMi**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.00329 "DoReMi: Grounding Language Model by Detecting and Recovering from Plan-Execution Misalignment") · 2023-07 · Tsinghua University — The LLM planner also emits constraints for each step; a VLM checks them continuously during low-level execution so plan-execution misalignments are caught immediately and the LLM replans. Shown on robot arms and humanoids. _Note: IROS 2024. No code link found on the project page._ [project](https://sites.google.com/view/doremi-paper)
- 🟢 [**REFLECT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15724 "REFLECT: Summarizing Robot Experiences for Failure Explanation and Correction") · 2023-06 · Columbia University — Converts multisensory robot logs into a hierarchical text summary that an LLM queries to explain why an execution failed and to guide a language planner's correction; introduces the RoboFail dataset of failure scenarios. _Note: CoRL 2023._ [code](https://github.com/columbia-ai-robotics/reflect) · [project](https://robot-reflect.github.io/)
- ⚪ [**SuccessVQA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.07280 "Vision-Language Models as Success Detectors") · 2023-03 · DeepMind — Frames success detection as visual question answering, fine-tuning a Flamingo VLM on human reward annotations; studied on simulated household agents, real robot manipulation and egocentric human video, with a focus on out-of-distribution generalisation.
